narrative:
Your application was denied because the model estimated a 37.0% probability that you would become a bad credit risk. In practical terms, it sees roughly a one-in-three chance of repayment difficulty; although that is not a majority, it was still above the bank’s acceptance cutoff for this application, so the loan was not approved.

The most influential factor in the decision was your checking-account status: a balance of at least 200 DM or salary. This worked in your favor and pushed the estimate toward good credit. The second most influential factor was your savings below 100 DM, which pushed toward bad credit and was the main adverse signal among the top three factors. The third was the furniture/equipment purpose of the loan, which worked slightly in your favor. So two of the strongest factors supported you, but your low savings increased the perceived risk, and the overall balance of your profile still left the estimated risk above the approval threshold.

To improve your chances next time, focus on building a savings buffer before reapplying, and ask the lender whether a smaller amount, shorter repayment period, or manual review would be considered. You should also request the specific decline reasons and check your credit report for errors. Maintaining your checking-account balance will remain helpful.
